'''Jerrold Bates Tunnell''' (September 16, 1950 – April 1, 2022) was a mathematician known for his work in [[number theory]]. He was an associate professor of mathematics at [[Rutgers University]].

==Early life and education==
Tunnell was born on September 16, 1950, in [[Dallas]], [[Texas]].<ref name="neal"/>

He graduated from [[Harvey Mudd College]] in 1972.<ref name="hmc-1">{{cite magazine |url=https://www.hmc.edu/mathematics/wp-content/uploads/sites/49/2017/07/v7n1.pdf |title=Benjamin, Pippenger, Klawe and alumni named to first class of AMS Fellows |magazine=mudd/math |volume=7 |issue=1 |publisher=[[Harvey Mudd College]] |year=2013 |pages=4–5 |accessdate=April 9, 2022}}</ref><ref name="RGS"/> He received his PhD in Mathematics from [[Harvard University]] in 1977.<ref name="IAS">{{cite web |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/jerrold-b-tunnell |title=Jerrold B. Tunnell |website=[[Institute for Advanced Study]] |date=December 9, 2019 |accessdate=April 9, 2022}}</ref><ref name="genealogy">{{MathGenealogy|id=6191|name=Jerrold B. Tunnell}}</ref><ref name="RGS"/> His thesis, ''On the Local Langlands Conjecture for GL(2)'', was advised by [[John Tate (mathematician)|John Tate]].<ref name="genealogy"/>

==Career==
After graduation, Tunnell taught at [[Princeton University]] and was a member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] from 1982 to 1983.<ref name="IAS"/><ref name="RGS"/> He joined the mathematics faculty at [[Rutgers University]] in 1983,<ref name="RGS"/> eventually becoming an associate professor of mathematics.<ref name="rutgers-profile">{{cite web |url=https://www.math.rutgers.edu/component/comprofiler/userprofile/tunnell?Itemid=831 |title=Jerrold Tunnell |website=[[Rutgers University]] |accessdate=April 9, 2022}}</ref> He advised 7 PhD students.<ref name="RGS"/>

==Research==
In 1981, Tunnell generalized Langlands' work on the [[Artin L-function#The Artin conjecture|Artin conjecture]], establishing a special case known as the Langlands–Tunnell theorem that later became a key component in the [[Wiles's proof of Fermat's Last Theorem|proof of Fermat's Last Theorem]].<ref>{{Cite journal |doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-1981-14936-3 |last=Tunnell |first=Jerrold |title=Artin's conjecture for representations of octahedral type |journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. |series=N. S. |volume=5 |year=1981 |issue=2 |pages=173–175 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last1=Prasad|first1=Dipendra |last2=Yogananda|first2=C. S. |editor1-last=Bambah|editor1-first=R. P.|editor2-last=Dumir|editor2-first=V. C.|editor3-last=Hans-Gill|editor3-first=R. J.|chapter=A Report on Artin's Holomorphy Conjecture|title=Number Theory|year=2000|publisher=Birkhäuser Basel|pages=301–314|isbn=978-3-0348-7023-8|doi=10.1007/978-3-0348-7023-8_16|url=http://www.math.tifr.res.in/~dprasad/artin.pdf}}</ref>

He proved [[Tunnell's theorem]] in 1983, which gives a partial unconditional solution to the [[congruent number problem]] and a complete solution conditional on the [[Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture]].<ref>{{cite journal
  | last = Tunnell
  | first = Jerrold B.
  | authorlink = Jerrold B. Tunnell
  | title = A classical Diophantine problem and modular forms of weight 3/2
  | journal = [[Inventiones Mathematicae]]
  | volume = 72
  | issue = 2
  | pages = 323–334
  | year = 1983
  | doi = 10.1007/BF01389327
  | bibcode = 1983InMat..72..323T
 | url = http://www.digizeitschriften.de/dms/img/?PID=GDZPPN002099403| hdl = 10338.dmlcz/137483
  | s2cid = 121099824
 | hdl-access = free
  }}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
In 2013, Tunnell was elected in the inaugural class of [[Fellow of the American Mathematical Society|Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |website=[[American Mathematical Society]] |accessdate=November 16, 2013 |archive-date=August 25, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Starting in 2004, Tunnell made cross-country cycling trips from [[Highland Park, New Jersey]], to [[Syracuse, New York]], in every U.S. election cycle.<ref name="hmc-2">{{cite magazine |url=https://www.hmc.edu/mathematics/wp-content/uploads/sites/49/2017/07/v7n1.pdf |title=Alumni news |magazine=mudd/math |volume=7 |issue=1 |publisher=[[Harvey Mudd College]] |year=2013 |pages=24–30 |accessdate=April 9, 2022}}</ref>

Tunnell died on April 1, 2022, in rural Texas.<ref name="neal">{{cite web |url=https://www.nealfh.net/obituary/Jerrold-Tunnell |website=Neal Funeral Home |title=Jerrold Tunnell |accessdate=April 9, 2022}}</ref><ref name="RGS">{{cite news |url=http://www.riograndesun.com/obituaries/jerrold-bates-tunnell/article_305fe482-bc45-11ec-8ee5-b7c3faaaefe4.html |title=Jerrold Bates Tunnell |work=[[Rio Grande Sun]] |date=April 15, 2022 |accessdate=April 18, 2022}}</ref> He was hit by a truck while riding his bicycle from [[St. Augustine, Florida]], to his 50th class reunion at [[Harvey Mudd College]] in [[Claremont, California]].<ref name="RGS"/>
